$comment: T-414: single machine-readable SoT for the prdt hook roster. install.sh §4 (jq --slurpfile) and packages/gui/electron/ipc/onboarding.ts (installPrdtHooks) both derive their ~/.claude/settings.json `hooks` registration from THIS file — neither hand-writes the event/matcher/order shape anymore. Edit here, not in either derived site. `basenames` is the flat roster (order = install.sh §1 mirror-copy order); `registrations` is the ordered list of {event, matcher?, hooks[]} entries each derivation reduces over, in registration order. `hooks[]` entries are basenames from ~/.prdt/hooks/ — install.sh prefixes `$PRDT_HOME/hooks/`, onboarding.ts prefixes the equivalent `<homeDir>/.prdt/hooks/`, both quoting the final command string. T-445: the discipline precedence is `canonical < machine override < project override`, and array order alone does NOT enforce it — measured 2026-08-12 on Claude Code 2.1.228, hooks sharing a matcher run in PARALLEL and their additionalContext blocks are appended in COMPLETION order (a 0.6s sleep in the machine hook made its block land AFTER the project block, registration order unchanged). Precedence is therefore carried by the payload TEXT: each override payload names its own layer and who outranks it. Keep prdt-overrides-inject.sh second-to-last and prdt-project-overrides-inject.sh last anyway — that is the intended order and the usual outcome — but never let position be the only carrier. T-491: the call governor is registered on TWO events, both MATCHER-LESS on purpose — it counts one API turn per PostToolBatch and enforces on every PreToolUse, so a tool matcher would make the count depend on WHICH tools a worker happened to use. The pair is atomic: registering the PreToolUse half without the PostToolBatch half leaves an enforcer reading a counter nothing increments, i.e. silent non-enforcement. Since §8 r6 measured that the harness accepts a typo'd event name with no error at all, the governor stamps a per-event fire marker under $PRDT_HOME/run/call-governor/ and `prdt doctor` reports an event registered here that has never fired. T-490: prdt-dispatch-gate.sh shares the PreToolUse event with the governor but carries the `Agent` matcher, and the two entries are NOT interchangeable — the governor must stay matcher-less (it counts turns across all tools) while the gate must stay matched (it parses a dispatch prompt, which only the Agent tool has). The matcher is also what keeps the gate off SendMessage: a resumed worker carries no `[ctx]` line by design, so widening this matcher would deny every resume. Keep the matcher-less governor entry FIRST among the PreToolUse entries — not a correctness requirement of either derivation (both group by event and replay in array order), but the intended reading order: the unconditional hook, then the narrowed one. Keep the four small inject hooks on the compact matcher too: without them a compaction re-injects the discipline set but silently drops audience-mode, plan-tier and BOTH override layers. T-490 slice 3: NEVER emit `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` from a hook registered on the SubagentStop entry — measured 2026-08-24 on harness 2.1.241, that context is injected into the WORKER and RESUMES it with no loop guard (one probe line produced 9 further SubagentStop firings, the worker itself echoing the injected token), so it reports to the wrong model AND burns worker turns. T-553: `{"decision":"block","reason":…}` on a SubagentStop hook's stdout is a DIFFERENT channel and is the one ALLOWED there — measured 2026-09-04 (2.1.260, 2/2) and re-measured 2026-09-09 (2.1.266): it resumes the worker ONCE, bounded by `stop_hook_active` (the harness's own loop guard — false on the first firing, true on the re-fire, so no state file of ours caps the retry), the worker re-emits its final message, and the parent receives only the last one. prdt-return-check.sh is the one hook that uses it: the worker return-envelope GATE (moved out of prdt-post-dispatch.sh, which is a state recorder and stays silent on SubagentStop). It validates the contracts §Return envelope floor where `last_assistant_message` is; a first violation is blocked with a reason naming the violation and the offending value, a clean return gets no output at all, and a return that still breaks on the re-fire is let through with a `reask: true` flag queued to `.prdt/.return-flags.json` for prdt-user-prompt.sh to render (UserPromptSubmit additionalContext, the channel T-498 r9 proved reaches the PO). PostToolUse additionalContext DOES reach the parent, but PostToolUse/Agent fires at LAUNCH for a background dispatch, with no return to inspect. A machine whose mirror predates T-553 keeps the advisory-only detector inside its old prdt-post-dispatch.sh — today's behaviour, not silence — until install.sh replaces both from this roster. T-577: prdt-session-start-p2..p12.sh are PART SLOTS of the discipline injection — one registered command per part, because the harness persists any single hook additionalContext over 10,000 chars to a file and injects only a 2,000-char preview (measured, Claude Code 2.1.260); the set is split into ≤8,000 B parts and every slot execs prdt-session-start.sh with its own part number. They ride every matcher part 1 rides (startup|resume|clear, compact via prdt-post-compact.sh, SubagentStart ^prdt-), right after it; a slot past the last needed part prints nothing. The slot count is the delivery CAPACITY (`prdt doctor` reports parts needed vs slots registered) — add a slot here AND as a byte-identical p<k>.sh file. T-677: prdt-secret-guard.sh registers on PreToolUse with the `Read|Bash` matcher — the two tool shapes that can print a credential file's bytes to the screen and into the session record (`Edit`/`Write`/`Grep` never reach it, by design: the matcher itself is the guarantee that WRITING a target file, or the Grep tool reading one, is never denied by this hook). It sits LAST among the PreToolUse entries, after the matcher-less governor and the `Agent`-matched dispatch gate — order changes neither derivation's behavior (both group by event and replay every matching entry in array order), but it keeps the same 'unconditional hook, then narrower ones' reading order T-490 already established for the gate. The hook runs a bash `case` PRE-FILTER on the raw event JSON before it ever calls jq: a miss — the overwhelming majority of Read/Bash calls, measured 557 hits out of several thousand real tool_use payloads on this machine — costs a fork-0 `case` match and nothing else, so adding this hook to every Read/Bash call stays cheap; jq runs only on the rare hit, to pull `tool_name`/`tool_input.file_path`/`tool_input.command`, and any jq absence or JSON/field failure fails OPEN (exit 0, silent) the same way every sibling hook on this roster already does — install.sh itself refuses to run without jq, so a machine that reaches this hook at all has it. The hook never reads `cwd` and applies with no prdt-project gate (T-684's answer): a credential file belongs to the USER, not to whichever project cwd happens to be under, and the hook's own registration is itself user-level (`~/.claude/settings.json`) — a cwd walk would only add cost and open a 'safe everywhere except this subdirectory' hole. T-682 slice 3: prdt-post-dispatch.sh is registered on SubagentStart as well — as its OWN second `^prdt-` entry, never appended to the discipline entry (that entry's shape is pinned: 16 commands, session-start first, project overrides LAST; both derivations emit one settings entry per registration, so a second entry with the same matcher is legal and leaves the precedence entry untouched; the hook prints nothing there): SubagentStart is the only mode-independent START signal of a dispatch (foreground: SubagentStart → SubagentStop → PostToolUse:Agent; background: SubagentStart → PostToolUse:Agent → SubagentStop — measured on 2.1.283), and the hook writes the in-flight marker the statusline's `running` segment reads there. A settings.json installed before this entry still records costs exactly as before; only the marker's start moves back to PostToolUse:Agent for background launches and is absent for foreground ones. T-779: prdt-worktree-guard.sh registers on PreToolUse with the `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash` matcher — the tool shapes that WRITE a file — as its own entry after the secret guard (same 'unconditional, then narrower' reading order). It denies a prdt-developer / prdt-qa worker whose OWN dispatch prompt carried `[ctx].worktree` a write under the shared code checkout; the worker's worktree comes from its own transcript's first prompt (keyed by the event's agent_id), else a run/dispatches marker whose `pairing` is `confirmed` (T-780) — an unconfirmed marker never denies. A fork-0 `case` on the raw payload skips every event that is not a developer/qa worker's before python3 runs; any failure fails OPEN. T-794: prdt-auto-open.sh gets a SECOND PostToolUse entry, matcher `Bash`, right after its existing `Write` entry (same script, same basename, one more registration — never a second file). The CLI (`prdt viewer` / `prdt tickets --link`) stopped opening anything itself, because a plain subprocess has no way to see who invoked it; only a registered hook event carries `agent_type` (or its absence). This entry is that hook: it reads a completed `prdt …` Bash call's own `tool_input.command` + `tool_response.stdout`, skips silently when `agent_type` is present (a worker's call) or the command has no `prdt` token or carries a literal `--no-open`, and otherwise re-invokes itself in `--open <path>` mode per `[label](file://…)` line found in the stdout — so every existing `--open` guard (GUI session, auto-open=off, the extension allowlist, T-571 warm-handler) applies unchanged, once per link. T-802: the same entry's matcher widens from `Write` to `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` — one background, coalesced `prdt viewer --no-open` per project root now fires on ANY docs/**/*.md write (PO or worker, Edit/MultiEdit included), independent of every opening guard the script still applies below it (GUI session, agent_type, auto-open=off none of those gate a background regen, only an actual `open`/`open -R` call) — never a second file, never a second registration: still the same basename, same script, one more tool shape on its existing Write entry.
